title: Label-free dopamine detection using Cu 2 O/Ag SERS substrates: effect of substrate architecture on molecular adsorption and SERS response
content: Substrate architecture strongly affects surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) because analyte adsorption must be spatially matched with plasmonic enhancement regions. In this work, AgNPs, an ex situ assembled Cu2O/Ag composite, and an in situ formed Cu2O/Ag hybrid were prepared, fabricated into the corresponding SERS substrates, and compared for label-free dopamine detection. Structural and optical characterization confirmed the formation of Ag-containing Cu2O/Ag nanostructures with different architectures: the composite retained distinguishable AgNP-like domains associated with Cu2O particles, whereas the hybrid showed a more compact and integrated morphology. Dopamine was used as the main target analyte, while thiram and methylene blue (MB) were used as probe molecules to evaluate analyte-dependent substrate behavior. The dopamine response followed the order Cu2O/Ag composite > AgNPs > Cu2O/Ag hybrid, indicating that Cu2O incorporation was beneficial only when Cu2O-assisted adsorption was coupled with accessible Ag-enhancing regions. In contrast, thiram showed the strongest response on AgNPs, confirming the importance of direct Ag–S interaction, while MB showed a trend closer to dopamine. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations supported these trends by showing catechol/OH-associated interaction of dopamine with Cu2O-like sites, dissociative sulfur-based adsorption of thiram, and Cu–N interaction of MB+. Using the Cu2O/Ag composite, dopamine was detected over 10−7–10−4 M with a calculated limit of detection of 2.16 × 10−8 M. The within-substrate and substrate-to-substrate RSD values were 12.04% and 13.34%, respectively, and calculated recoveries of 95–105% were obtained in an artificial urine matrix. These results demonstrate that the Cu2O/Ag composite is a simple label-free SERS platform for dopamine detection, with preliminary evaluation in an artificial urine matrix, with performance governed by the balance between Cu2O-assisted adsorption and accessible Ag-based enhancement.
